paper_title: MPIE-Bench: Benchmarking Anatomically Plausible Multi-Person Interaction Editing

sections.title: Abstract
sections.content: Text-to-image and personalized editing models now synthesize high-fidelity single-subject images with ease. Yet placing multiple named people into shared contact actions such as embrace, carry, or grapple still exposes major failures: fused limbs, invented extremities, and interpenetrating bodies. Existing evaluations largely overlook these anatomical and geometric issues, and VLM-as-a-judge checklists often saturate on Interaction while the errors remain obvious to humans. We introduce MPIE-Bench, a 2,500-sample benchmark of video-mined editing triplets spanning 405 scenes, 14 interaction categories, and four contact densities (C0-C3). We also propose MPIE-Eval, whose two new axes score contact-time geometry from a frozen public multi-person mesh reconstruction. Anatomy asks whether every human-like mass is explained by a complete set of reconstructed bodies, and Interaction asks whether the penetration and surface distance between those bodies match the contact the instruction asked for. Across ten editors, mesh Anatomy tops out at 0.65 and mesh Interaction at 0.72 on two different models, so no single editor is strong on both, while VLM checklists rate the same images above 0.95. A five-rater study confirms that both axes track human judgement more closely than a zero-shot VLM judge, and the rankings hold under ablation of every weight and threshold.

sections.title: 1 Introduction
sections.content: Text-to-image models now compose coherent scene from short instruction, follow directions about layout and style, and carry named persons appearance from few reference photographs into new image. Demand is moving toward scenes where several people interact: two friends embracing, parent carrying child, two athletes grappling. Even the strongest models break down here, and not in the way current benchmarks look for. The people stay recognizable and so does the requested action; what fails is the body. Limbs fuse where two people touch, extra hands and feet appear along the contact seam, and one body occupies the volume of another (Figure 3). Current evaluation cannot see this. Benchmarks for multi-person and personalized generation ask how many people appear, whether their identities match the references, whether the requested action is present, and how pleasing the result looks (Borse et al., 2025; Xu et al., 2026; Peng et al., 2026), and an image whose bodies are anatomically impossible satisfies all four. The suites that do ask about interaction often delegate that judgement to vision-language model (Peng et al., 2026), which in our experiments rates the strongest closed-source models between 0.98 and 0.99 on interaction quality for images whose fused limbs are obvious to human reader. Whether the requested edit happened and whether the bodies survived it are different questions, and only the first is being asked. Table 1 summarizes the gap. We close it with MPIE-Bench, benchmark for multi-person interaction editing, and MPIE-Eval, protocol that derives contact-time body coherence from 3D human mesh reconstruction rather than from language models opinion. Data comes first, since images of people in dense physical contact are rare in personalization corpora. We therefore mine video, where frames in which the people stand apart crop into per-person identity references and later frame in dense contact serves as held-out target from the same real interaction. contact-density curve locates those valleys and peaks, vision-language model writes the edit instruction backwards from the pair, and human review leaves 2,500 triplets over 405 scenes, 14 interaction categories 1 and four contact densities, as the MPIE-Bench section details. Scoring them is where our main contribution lies. MPIE-Eval reconstructs the people in generated image with frozen, publicly available multi-person mesh recovery model and reads two axes off those meshes. Anatomy asks whether every human-like mass is explained by complete set of reconstructed bodies, which is precisely what fused or invented limb is not. Interaction asks whether penetration and surface distance between those bodies match the contact the instruction asked for. The two join the conventional Count, Identity, Instruction and Quality axes and are never blended into single number; because the frontend and every threshold are fixed in advance, any ranking can be recomputed from released dumps (Figure 1). Across ten closedand open-source editors, mesh Anatomy tops out at 0.65 and mesh Interaction at 0.72 on two different models, so no single editor is strong on both, while checklist judge rates the same images above 0.95. Five-rater human gold confirms that the mesh axes track people more closely than that judge on hard contact items, and the ranking survives ablation of every weight and threshold. Contributions. 1. MPIE-Bench: licensing-aware mining pipeline and frozen public test set whose references and target come from the same real interaction, stratified by interaction category and contact density. 2. MPIE-Eval: Anatomy and Interaction axes that score contact-time limb completeness and body interpenetration from frozen public mesh frontend, with every band and weight fixed before scoring. 3. complete human-consistency study establishing that the protocol is accurate and robust, against five-rater human gold, against zero-shot VLM judge, and under ablation of every weight, gate and threshold.

sections.title: 2 Related Work
sections.content: Multi-person generation and editing. Personalized generation began with adapters and spatial conditions binding one identity into scene. Group-level editing followed, and the field consolidated around multireference in-context editors that take several references and an instruction in single passthe interface we evaluate (Borse et al., 2025; Xu et al., 2026; Gu and Yang, 2026; Peng et al., 2026; Jiang et al., 2024; Li et al., 2026b; Wu et al., 2026b; Wang et al., 2025b; Chen et al., 2026a). Identity preservation and instruction following improve quickly along this line; close-contact geometry does not. Benchmarks for generation and editing. Evaluation followed one step behind: human-aligned protocols for subject-driven generation, large instruction-editing datasets, and the first suites for generating several recognizable humans (Ye et al., 2025; Jiang et al., 2026; Brooks et al., 2023; Peng et al., 2025; Huang et al., 2024; Luo et al., 2026; Nguyen et al., 2026; Borse et al., 2025). Interaction itself entered through stress tests that use physical contact to break identity binding, diagnostics for attribute ownership, and concurrent preference-based interaction binding (Peng et al., 2026; Chen et al., 2026a; Nguyen et al., 2026). In every case the interaction question is semantic or relational, never whether the bodies realizing that relation remain anatomically possible. Judging bodies, and judging the judges. parallel line asks whether generated body is possible at all, 2 from annotated synthetic anatomical defects to learned realism metrics that feed single-image 3D body representation into predictor (Fang et al., 2024a; Li et al., 2026a; Andreou et al., 2024; Käs et al., 2026). Purpose-built detectors then found that general vision-language models sit near chance at localizing missing or redundant body parts. All of this work, the reconstruction-assisted metric included, is scoped to single isolated person. As Table 1 shows, multi-person suites still omit joint anatomical completeness and interaction geometry, and VLM scores on contact axes often stay near ceiling. MPIE targets this gap with contact-rich editing triplets and mesh-based Anat/Inter (Figure 1). Interaction-aware geometry and HMR. Multi-person HMR (Baradel et al., 2024; Brégier et al., 2025; Zheng et al., 2026), contact-field representations (Lee et al., 2024), hand reconstruction (Pavlakos et al., 2024), and related contact/distance machinery (Wang et al., 2025a; Fang et al., 2024b; Saha et al., 2025) make geometry-side scoring feasible. For the public v1 protocol we freeze single RGB Multi-HMR frontend so editor rankings are reproducible; stronger contact-aware reconstructors can be swapped in later as alternate leaderboard tracks.

sections.title: 3 MPIE-Bench
sections.content: Figure 1 MPIE-Bench / MPIE-Eval overview. (A) data construction; (B) six-axis eval with mesh Anat/Inter. Figure 1(A) sketches construction; Figure 1(B) and MPIE-Eval below define scoring. Sources. We collect multi-person interaction videos from three open sources: permissively licensed Pexels stock footage, Harmony4D (Khirodkar et al., 2024), and CHI3D (Fieraru et al., 2020). Stock supplies identity and scene diversity; studio sources add hard contact with persistent actor labels. We filter for resolution and multi-person presence, categorize by interaction type, and exclude restricted-tier corpora from the redistributable split. related CHI3D interaction resource (Fieraru et al., 2025) is used only to calibrate mesh soft bands on held-out GT reconstructions in MPIE-Eval below; it contributes neither MPIE-Bench test scenes nor any Table 3 generator output. Inputoutput selection. Contact-sparse frames yield clean per-person references; contact-dense frames yield interaction targets. For each video we compute contact-density curve ϕ(t) from person-box IoU, pose proximity, optical flow, and occlusion cues, with refine mix 0.35/0.30/0.20/0.15 after within-video percentile norm. Local maxima of smoothed ϕ with height P60 and 2 gap yield peak targets; disjoint high-separation pool yields valley references. When multi-person 3D poses are available, peaks/valleys use nearest-joint distance instead. References follow cross-video > cross-shot > cross-camera > same-shot priority to mitigate 3 copy-paste leakage (Chen et al., 2026b). This valleypeak construction is the operational definition of an editing sample: references are easy-to-crop people, and the target is harder interaction frame from the same scene narrative, not random collage. Prompt reverse writing. Given valley references {Rk} and the peak target, VLM reverse-captions an edit instruction that names roles, the shared action, and contact intent, without revealing target pixels at test time. Contact intent is later mapped to {required, forbidden, unspecified} for Interaction mixing (Section 4.4); the prompt text itself remains the only instruction shown to editors. Human review and distribution. Automatic mining yields 20,000 candidates. Adult reviewers remove unsafe or off-task clips, check that each reverse-captioned prompt names the visible interaction, then de-duplicate and cap per scene to freeze 2,500 targets across 405 scenes. Coverage is 144 grid: fourteen everyday-tocombat interaction categories crossed with four contact-density levels, from no contact through hand-level and torso/point-line contact up to high contact (Figure 2); about 61% of samples sit in the two denser bins. Stock footage supplies most targets (2,135); studio CHI3D/Harmony4D add hard-contact coverage, with about 3.2 references per sample on average. Most prompts expect two people (2,093 samples); 399 samples (16%) expect three or more, up to nine. Splits are scene-level, and reference embeddings freeze at finalize. Valleypeak may change camera or background within scene; we score this as reference-conditioned interaction editing under that gap, not as pixel-local inpainting. Figure 2 Public test-set distribution (N =2,500). Inner ring: contact density from none (C0) to high contact (C3); outer ring: 14 interaction categories.

sections.title: 4 MPIE-Eval
sections.content: MPIE-Eval reports six axes separately and never blends them into one scalar. Count, Identity, Instruction, and Quality ask whether the edit request was met; Anatomy and Interaction ask whether bodies stay coherent at contact. Figure 1(B) sketches the pipeline: reconstruct people once, then score Anatomy from unexplained mass and Interaction from pairwise contact geometry, while the four task axes stay on their own tracks.

sections.title: 4.1 Why mesh scores for contact geometry
sections.content: VLM checklists often report success on contact while fused limbs and interpenetration remain obvious (Figure 3). 2D rubric can confirm that two people are hugging, yet miss whether limb is invented or one mesh volume occupies another. We therefore score Anatomy and Interaction from frozen 3D human reconstruction frontend (Baradel et al., 2024): one public stack for all editors, released dumps for audit, and transparent geometric proxies rather than another preference head. The resulting scores are ranking observables, not physical volumes; soft bands and mix weights below are public and were locked before scoring the ten editors.

sections.title: 4.3 Anatomy
sections.content: Anatomy asks whether every human-like region in the image is explained by complete set of people. We group failures into four readable families and score each from 1 (clean) to 0 (severe): Extra / fused limbs: mass glued onto person that should not be there. Floating parts: detached leftover blobs that belong to no body. Body structure: broken scale, part ownership, or self-collision on the meshes. Residual mass: leftover human-like foreground not covered above. To detect the first two families we compare classical human-like foreground mask (luma/saturation vs. the border; no learned segmenter) with raster of the kept meshes inside padded person ROI. Their mismatch is the leftover fraction ℓ = Mfg Mex Mfg , and we also count detached leftover blobs nb. When leftover is high but no blob floats free (ℓ0.62, nb=0), we treat it as an attached false limb rather than clothing clutter; otherwise attach terms are down-weighted so loose clothing does not dominate. Each diagnostic maps through the same soft ramp s(x; a, b) = clip((b x)/(b a), 0, 1) (good below a, fail above b). Within family we keep the worst sub-score, then mix the four family scores with public weights

sections.title: 4.5 Protocol freeze and calibration
sections.content: Table 2 lists the public freeze used for Table 3. Soft Interaction bands are fit on held-out CHI3D-related GT reconstructions (Fieraru et al., 2025) with no MPIE-Bench test scenes and no generator outputs from the leaderboard: volume/distance cutoffs target GT percentiles so typical contact lies in the soft-ok band and rare extremes approach fail. We release the recipe and dumps, not restricted calibration pixels. Two resolution tracks share the same algebra: Track at vendor-native resolution and Track after letterbox10242 (Tables 3/6).

sections.title: 4.6 Task axes
sections.content: We also report four established axes so rankings stay comparable and Anatomy/Interaction cannot be gamed alone. Two VLM paths are kept separate: shared geometry checklist (vlm_judge) and per-sample Instruction QA bank. Count. Binary person-count correctness from the shared vlm_judge checklist, using the same call family as the V-Anat/V-Inter baseline in Experiments, not the Instruction bank. Identity. Occlusion-aware face matching to frozen reference embeddings with one-to-one assignment and yaw gate (Borse et al., 2025; Xu et al., 2026); GT-visible faces that disappear score zero. Instruction. separate pipeline from vlm_judge: for each of the 2,500 samples we freeze small atomic QA set offline from the edit text alone covering role, asymmetry, and prop. At eval time VLM only answers on the generation; it cannot invent questions. Quality. Standard human-preference aesthetic score (Wu et al., 2023), reported raw and never mixed into Anatomy/Interaction.

sections.title: 5.3 Metric validation of Anat/Inter
sections.content: Our metric contribution is Anatomy and Interaction; Count, Identity, Instruction, and Quality follow standard practice. Prior multi-person suites that address contact typically use VLM or semantic probe  (Table 1)  . We validate mesh Anat/Inter by controlled corruptions and by human agreement against that VLM-style baseline. Sanity checks. The hull penetration term is ranking proxy rather than physical volume. sections.title: 6 Conclusion
sections.content: We set out to make contact-time body coherence measurable for multi-person interaction editing. MPIE-Bench contributes licensing-aware, scene-split test set of 2,500 video-mined triplets over 405 scenes, stratified by 14 interaction categories and C0C3 contact density, with held-out targets so editors cannot copy pixels. MPIE-Eval contributes six-axis protocol that keeps Count/ID/Instruction/Quality for task success while scoring Anatomy/Interaction from frozen, dump-auditable Multi-HMR frontend under dual public tracks: Track at vendor-native resolution and Track after letterbox10242. Across ten editors, the mesh axes do work the checklists do not: closed V-Inter saturates near ceiling while M-Inter retains dynamic range; identity remains the steepest closed/open gap; Anat and Inter leaders need not coincide; and density, corruption, human-checklist, and ablation checks support model-level ranking under the frozen frontend rather than single blended score. We release the redistributable subset, evaluation code, per-sample Multi-HMR dumps, and the calibration recipe so the community can audit rankings and add alternate-frontend tracks without redefining the editing task.

sections.title: A Extended protocol notes
sections.content: Instr v2 design. We separate question generation from answering. Offline, text-only stage extracts atomic claims from the edit instruction and freezes per-sample QA bank with buckets role/asymm/prop (main) and optional scene (diagnostic only), forbidding interaction-occurrence, count, face-identity, and anatomy questions. At evaluation time the VLM answers the frozen questions from the generated image alone and cannot rewrite them. An earlier image-conditioned self-authored instr_qa protocol saturated on closed-source models and is deprecated. Mesh Interaction intent. Contact intent is read from the edit prompt text (not the dataset category label), yielding required / forbidden / unspecified. Penalties combine interpenetration volume, enclosure fraction, proximity, and contact-quality terms , with soft ramps calibrated on GT frames. The metric flags unreasonable geometry; higher Inter than GT can occur when generation under-penetrates relative to real contact. Release artifacts. We release: (i) the redistributable test subset and scene-level split; (ii) frozen reference face embeddings; (iii) evaluation scripts for the six-axis protocol including 3D mesh Anatomy/Interaction; (iv) the human checklist template and agreement scripts; (v) the metric calibration recipe for GT percentile thresholds. Toward anatomy-aware training (future work) The main paper is evaluation-only. For completeness we sketch training recipe we are exploring on top of MPIE-Bench signals; none of these results are required to use the benchmark. Base model. Fine-tune FLUX.1 Kontext (Labs et al., 2025) with rank-512 LoRA rather than full-parameter updates, because (a) narrow-task data at 104 scale risks catastrophic forgetting under full fine-tuning of large DiT, and (b) Kontext is guidance-distilled; full updates can disturb the distillation structure. Kontext already exposes native reference-conditioning pathway, so we do not add an identity encoder unless post-hoc ID/MCP diagnostics indicate copy-paste cheating. Auxiliary skeleton stream. lightweight auxiliary LoRA + projection head predicts 2D multi-person skeleton visualization during training (discarded at inference), encouraging the shared backbone to keep one complete skeleton per person under occlusion targeting limb-fusion and limb-attribution failures. Contact-density curriculum. Training samples are scheduled along C0C3: early C0C1, mid C2, late C3, so the model stabilizes body completeness before deep mutual occlusion. This is dataloader-level change with zero architectural cost. What we defer. Corrupted positive/negative pairs from metric calibration are reserved for future preference optimization / RL stages (e.g., Diffusion-DPO (Wallace et al., 2024), Flow-GRPO (Liu et al., 2025)) rather than standard supervised losses that would simply reproduce corruptions. 13 VLM-as-judge saturation diagnostic An all-checklist visual judge yields Anatomy/Interaction means near 0.980.99 for strong closed-source editors while fused limbs and pathological interpenetration remain visible. Parametric joint/bone priors similarly saturate ( 0.99) because hallucinated extremities often lie outside the fitted topology. Primary tables therefore report mesh-anchored Anatomy and prompt-conditioned Interaction in 3D mesh space; checklist Anat/Inter remain diagnostics only and are released with the evaluation code rather than used for ranking.
